messages:
Maya: quick sync - need to finalize scope for cross-region routing pilot (Q2). customers want tenant-level isolation but we need to hit a cost target. tradeoffs?
Alejandra: two patterns we've been iterating on: 1) hard isolation \"lanes\" (perfect isolation, higher infra) 2) soft slices w/ prioritized scheduling + fallbacks (cheaper, more complex routing).
Sam: finance asked for <=15% uplift vs current baseline for the pilot. can soft slices meet that?
Alejandra: rough sim says soft slices ~10-12% uplift if we add prefix KV caching + smarter placement. lanes are ~30% uplift.
John L: public enterprise ask: some tenants will require regional SLAs and 5s cross-region failover. those will likely need dedicated lanes.
Maya: sounds like we need tiering. propose Tier-1 = dedicated lanes + regional affinity; Tier-2 = soft-slice + priority queueing + fallback variants.
Sam: agree. what are minimal launch gates for a sandbox pilot?
Maya: MVG (minimal viable gateway) should include: 1) routing-policy API (assign tenant->policy) 2) simple console view for tier assignment 3) fallback rules (model variant & region) 4) telemetry for failovers and fallback rates.
Alejandra: and add measurable SLO gates: p95 latency Tier-1 < 120ms, successful cross-region failover test in canary, and cost uplift validated against projection.
John L: also add canary rollback criteria: if fallback_count / total_requests > 5% for 1h, rollback. if cold-start rate spikes > 8% for Tier-1, rollback.
Sam: implementation notes: infra team prefers a routing table approach keyed by tenant label + policy. I'll put together an RFC with config schema and cost sim.
Maya: example policy sketch please include in RFC.
Sam: here's a tiny snippet that'll go in RFC:
```
routing_policies:
  - tenant: tenant-42
    tier: tier1
    affinity: region-us-west-2
    fallback: cheap-variant-v1
    kv_cache: enabled
```
I'll attach the cost model and sensitivity analysis.
Alejandra: timeline? customer pilot expected end of Q2. can dev deliver?
Maya: yes if we scope MVP narrow: no per-tenant KMS for MVP, no new billing primitives. focus on routing, fallback, telemetry.
John L: note from compliance: private deployments must be able to opt tenants into forced dedicated lanes. mark that as a must-have for private rollout, but non-blocking for hosted pilot.
SRE-bot: infra: canary cluster provisioning queued (REQ-1520). ETA 72h.
Sam: action items: RFC (Sam), cost model + sensitivity (Sam + Finance), canary infra (SRE), telemetry dashboard + failover metrics (Maya), pilot plan + customer comms (Alejandra).
Maya: I'll book 30m decision meeting Thursday to finalize tier definitions and gating metrics. please review RFC before then.
Alejandra: I'll draft pilot success criteria and a short FAQ for customers.
John L: one more ask - include a toggle in config to force model-variant fallback to be synchronous vs async for critical tenants (sync preferred for predictability).
Sam: noted - will include sync/async fallback option in RFC. RFC link when ready: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/1771 (will post here).
Maya: great. thanks everyone.
Alejandra: thanks! :thumbsup:
Sam: posting RFC in channel when ready.
